name: áes dána

attributes.attribute: Old Irish term that today names celebrated artists in Ireland
derived from the Old Irish word for poets
also applied to druids, brehons, and lawyers
gave the gift of inspiration to those who drank from it
its flesh passed on inspiration to those who tasted it

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Áes dána is an Old Irish phrase. Today in Ireland it names the country's most celebrated artists. The term began as the Old Irish word for poets. It also covered druids, brehons, and lawyers. A seeker gained inspiration by drinking from the Well of wisdom. One could eat the hazel nuts floating in it. Or one could eat of the salmon that swam in that water.

okr.objective: Áes dána is the Old Irish phrase for poets and artists.
key_results: Today áes dána names a group of celebrated artists in Ireland.
The term derives from the Old Irish word for poets.
It also applied to druids, brehons, and lawyers.
Inspiration came from the Well of wisdom, its hazel nuts, or the salmon in it.
okr.evidence: Monaghan, Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore

objective: To explain the meaning and origin of the Irish phrase áes dána.
key_results: In modern Ireland the phrase means a group of nationally acclaimed artists.
It derives from the Old Irish term for poets.
It was also applied to Druids, Brehons, or lawyers.
Inspiration came from the Well of wisdom, its hazel nuts, or the salmon that swam in it.
In Old Irish the áes dána were the learned classes who shaped the common literary language.
evidence: The phrase áes dána derives from the Old Irish term for poets and was also applied to Druids, Brehons, or lawyers.
